evidence.excerpt: A repeated-batch fermentation process for alkaline protease production using Aspergillus niger was operated over 12 consecutive batches in 5 L stirred-tank bioreactors. Protease activity in the harvest broth fell from 342 U/mL in batch 1 to 198 U/mL in batch 12, representing a 42% decline. Spent broth samples from each batch were profiled by HPLC-DAD for organic acids, amino acids, and sugar alcohols. Principal component analysis separated batches 1–4, 5–8, and 9–12 into distinct metabolic groups. Accumulation of gluconic acid (rising from 0.8 g/L to 4.1 g/L across batches) and concurrent depletion of free glutamate were the strongest discriminating variables. Spore morphology by light microscopy showed progressive conidiophore shortening correlating with gluconic acid concentration. The data suggest that acid accumulation combined with nitrogen recycling inefficiency drives the observed yield trajectory.
